bullets: Game 6 of 6 in a deck-showcase video (readable 1325.0s-1569.9s, clock opens at 2:55). All eight cards were confirmed by in-game deploy labels during the window; nothing costs more than 4 elixir.

The plan is a chip race: Wall Breakers at the left bridge tiles [4,14]/[3,14] (clock 1:18, 0:57, 0:38) backed by Magic Archer at [5,14] and Archers (clock 1:39) took the enemy left tower from 4527 to 2536 while the opponent committed to the right lane.

Defence is the Bomb Tower on a single centred tile [8,10] every time (clock 2:25, 1:03, 0:12, OT 1:47), fed with Skeletons, Fire Spirit and Bats; in regular time that held an Electro Giant + Graveyard + Miner deck to 80 HP of tower damage.

The deck out-damaged the opponent all game but could not close: at 0:00 in regular time the towers read 4858/4778 to 2078/2357, so it went to overtime, where the enemy right-lane Electro Giant push finally took his right tower 4778 -> 1615 while he took the enemy left tower to 298 and the right to 676. The video ends (1562-1568s outro) before any tower falls, so the result is unknown.
Commentary in this game is a balance-change review, not deck talk — the only card of his own he discusses is the Bomb Tower, as an example for the Hero Tombstone sight-range nerf (1349-1356s).

new_deck.rationale: Average elixir 2.375 with no card above 4, built around cycling cheap Wall Breakers pairs behind a Bomb Tower rather than around a single big push.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Wall Breakers are the only win condition, and at 2 elixir in a 2.4-elixir deck they can be sent at the bridge faster than most decks can rotate an answer. Bomb Tower placed dead centre in front of the King's Tower covers both lanes at once, which is what let this deck hold an Electro Giant, a Graveyard and a Miner to 80 HP of tower damage across all of regular time. Skeletons, Fire Spirit and Bats are the cheap bodies that keep the Bomb Tower alive and reset pushes, while Magic Archer and Archers at the river turn every defensive stop into left-lane chip. The weakness showed in overtime: with only one building and no reset spell for a supported tank, a repeated Electro Giant push eventually ground the right tower down.
